**How it works:** Rust allows `/* ... */` comments to be nested inside each other, but C++ doesn't.
- The file starts with `/* /* */`. C++ sees a complete comment, so it compiles the C++ code that follows. Rust sees two openings and only one closing, so it treats that C++ code as part of a comment.
- After the C++ code comes `#if 0`, so C++ skips everything up to `#endif`. Next is a `*/` line, which closes Rust's comment, so Rust compiles the code that follows.
- After the Rust code there's another `/* /* */`. It hides `#endif` from Rust, while C++ still sees it.
- The final line, `// */`, closes Rust's comment. C++ reads it as a one-line comment.

**Large N:** both versions do the addition one decimal digit at a time instead of using fixed-size integers. That means the answer doesn't overflow for big N.

My first version failed to compile under g++ with "unterminated #if". Changing the `/*` after the Rust code to `/* /* */` fixed it.
